title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine got no warning before Russian strike
excerpt: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine received no advance warning before the first wave of an overnight Russian attack on energy infrastructure. Officials also reported a death in Kyiv and widespread outages.
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that Russia launched overnight attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure with ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, and that Kyiv received no advance warning from partner countries before the first wave.

“Once again, Russia launched a ballistic missile attack in multiple waves throughout the night, and once again, there was no warning from our partners,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media, according to The Guardian. The news outlet also quoted Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat as saying Ukraine had not been warned before the first wave of strikes that hit power plants in Kyiv at around 11 p.m. Sunday.

Later, Zelenskyy said the barrage struck 28 substations and other critical energy facilities, leaving more than a half-million people without electricity, heat and running water, the New York Post reported. NBC News also reported that Zelenskyy said the attacks damaged more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities across the country.

Officials in Kyiv said a 21-year-old woman was killed in the capital, according to the New York Post, NBC News and the Los Angeles Times. Zelenskyy also said Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region.

The accounts differ on what happened before the second wave of strikes. The Guardian said Ihnat told television viewers that Ukraine did receive a warning before a successive strike at 3 a.m. The New York Post and the Los Angeles Times reported that information about the second wave arrived too late for air raid sirens to be activated in time.

The Russian Defense Ministry said it struck targets including a data center, a logistics hub storing components for drones and cruise missiles, an industrial facility making drone components and a locomotive depot where missiles are stored, according to the New York Post, NBC News and the Los Angeles Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday he had no information about the previous night’s attack. The Guardian quoted Rubio as saying, “If it happened last night, I don’t know exactly. I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system.”

Zelenskyy has been pressing for continued Western support as Washington and Kyiv have clashed over military aid and intelligence sharing. In the same social media post, he said, “Ukraine never wanted this war, and we have welcomed literally EVERY attempt by our partners to bring this war to a dignified end. We have responded positively to EVERY ceasefire proposal.” He added: “The reality is that the war continues, and it continues solely because of Russian strikes and Russia’s desire to drag this war out.”

Ukraine has also complained about slowed deliveries of American weapons and limits on the military-grade version of SpaceX’s Starlink service used by Ukrainian forces. On Sunday, Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, setting fire to an oil export terminal and a depot in St. Petersburg, according to NBC News and the New York Post.

sources.name: New York Post
sources.title: Zelensky says Ukraine received no warning from partners as Russia hits power grid again
key_facts: Russia launched new attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, adding that Kyiv again received no early warning of the attack from partner countries that previously shared their intelligence.
Zelenskyy is grappling with recent Washington moves benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin, including waiving U.S. sanctions on Moscow and signing a deal to import diesel from Moscow.
The Russian nighttime barrage hit 28 substations and other critical energy facilities, depriving more than a half-million people of electricity, heat and running water, Zelensky said on social media.

“The reality is that the war continues, and it continues solely because of Russian strikes and Russia’s desire to drag this war out.”
Ukraine has held back Moscow’s forces on the front line and has hit back with long-range strikes deep inside Russia on oil refineries that triggered fuel shortages.

U.S. and Russian officials said Monday that talks are continuing on the possibility of a trilateral meeting involving Putin, Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at an APEC summit in China next month to try to negotiate a deal on Ukraine, without Kyiv’s participation.

Ukraine did receive a warning before a successive strike, at 3am, Ihnat added.

“Once again, Russia launched a ballistic missile attack in multiple waves throughout the night, and once again, there was no warning from our partners,” Zelenskyy wrote in a social media post on Monday morning.
Ukraine has also complained of slowed deliveries of PAC-3 air defence missiles from the US.
However, Ukraine has said it was not warned on at least three days in the past week before missiles were launched, amid a public quarrel between Zelenskyy and Trump.

background.fact: 2026-10-18: Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, setting fire to an oil export terminal and a depot in St. Petersburg.
2026-10-17: Trump waived a sanctions package on Russia; packets frame this as part of recent Washington moves seen in Kyiv as benefiting Moscow.
At the end of the previous week, full Starlink service was being restored, but Zelenskyy said Monday that speed restrictions were still slowing Ukrainian drones at points along the front line.
Packets say a recent truce covering energy infrastructure that Trump had demanded had failed.

conflicts: Packets 1 and 4 say the barrage hit '28 substations and other critical energy facilities,' while packet 3 says it damaged 'more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities.'

Packet 2 says Ukraine did receive a warning before the successive 3 a.m. strike, while packets 1 and 4 say information about the second wave arrived too late for air raid sirens to be activated in time.
unverified: Packet 2 suggests Washington may be withholding intelligence 'in order to bully Kyiv into capitulating to Moscow'; that motive is not established by the packets.
Rubio’s reference to a 'software problem' in the early warning system appears only in packet 2 and is not independently substantiated in the other packets.

Packet 2 says the Trump administration reportedly threatened Kyiv with a slowdown in weapons deliveries unless it stopped striking Russian oil refineries; that is not corroborated elsewhere in the packets.
missing_evidence: Independent confirmation of the exact number and locations of energy facilities hit.
A definitive official timeline for the first and second waves of strikes and when, if at all, warnings were transmitted.
Clarification from the U.S. or other partner countries about why no advance warning was provided before the first wave.
Updated casualty and damage figures beyond the reported death of a 21-year-old woman.
Status of restoration of electricity, heat and running water for the affected population.
